author: Vox
description:
As data centers rapidly expand across the country to support the AI revolution, some Democrats are calling for a temporary halt to new construction. Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed tells Vox’s Astead Herndon why he is sympathetic to local moratoriums, but believes federal regulation is the real solution.

Watch the full conversation this Saturday on Vox’s YouTube channel.

author: Vox
description:
F1 races are exhilarating. While racing alongside 21 other cars, an F1 driver can reach speeds of up to 231 mph, making it one of the world's most dangerous sports.

And F1 drivers need to be physically prepared to prevent disaster. Over the course of a single race, they experience hundreds of pounds of force, temperatures up to 130°F, and risk extreme dehydration which can lead to lowered brain function. In order to stay on the road and not pass out, F1 drivers have to be in peak physical condition. 

In order to find out how F1 drivers can survive a sport that is so physically demanding, Vox producer Nate Krieger hit the gym. Since F1 is such an international sport, there aren’t many specialized trainers in the US. So with the help of an F1 performance expert currently based in the United Arab Emirates, Nate worked out with David Dunlop, a strength and conditioning coach who works with NFL players.
